text:
maria: Seeing a spike of failed GPU node bootstraps in ap-southeast-1. ~40% of provisioning attempts are failing with KMS AccessDenied and intermittent connection refused to our keystore proxy. Started seeing errors around 2171234500.
ajay: can you paste the bootstrap snippet / logs?
maria: ```
[2026-03-18T08:15:12Z] ERROR: decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/gpu-node-keystore is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt on resource arn:aws:kms:ap-southeast-1:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01
Caused by: connection refused (10.0.5.12:4000)
```
infra-bot: autoscaler alert: fallback-to-on-demand triggered in ap-southeast-1 — 25 on-demand nodes launched in last 20m. Estimated incremental cost: ~$3.1k.
zach: we pushed a NACL tighten yesterday to remediate an outbound port scan detected during PCI prep. We blocked ephemeral ports (32768-61000) outbound on the ap-southeast-1 node subnets — that will break kubelet/metadata/keystore flows which rely on ephemeral src ports.
maria: confirmed tcp 32768-61000 were denied by nacl-0abc123 (ap-southeast-1a/node-subnet). I can repro locally: curl to keystore via NAT from ephemeral port gets RST.
elena: i also saw an IAM tweak on the gpu-node-keystore role: added a Condition IpAddress on kms:Decrypt limiting calls to the VPC CIDR. Our keystore uses a NAT/privatelink pair so the source IP can be outside that CIDR. Combined with the NACL block this creates a perfect storm.
sec-ops: we applied the NACL change after the scanner flagged outbound wide-range sockets; we can add a narrow exception for bootstrap traffic but need a justification and an expiry window.
ajay: mitigation plan: (1) open ephemeral outbound range 32768-61000 on nacl-0abc123 for now, (2) add a temp tag `temp-allow-boot` with expiry=2171238200, (3) either relax the IAM IpAddress condition for `gpu-node-keystore` or add the privatelink endpoint IPs into the condition. Rollback automated after expiry.
maria: terraform patch (ready to apply):
```hcl
resource "aws_network_acl_rule" "allow_ephemeral_boot" {
  network_acl_id = "nacl-0abc123"
  rule_number    = 100
  egress         = true
  protocol       = "6"
  rule_action    = "allow"
  cidr_block     = "0.0.0.0/0"
  from_port      = 32768
  to_port        = 61000
  tags = { temporary = "true" expiry = "2171238200" }
}
```
and IAM diff (remove IpAddress condition on kms:Decrypt for role gpu-node-keystore) 
```json
- "Condition": { "IpAddress": { "aws:SourceIp": ["10.0.0.0/16"] } }
+ // remove IpAddress condition OR add privatelink egress IPs here
```
ops_sre: i'll apply the NACL change first (low risk) and retest bootstrapping. tagging this incident and will follow the expiry plan.
infra-bot: cost update: refined estimate — additional spend due to fallbacks and cross-zone data: ~$3.2k last hour.
elena: need an audit trail for the NACL/IAM changes. cloudtrail shows `security-admin@redwood` modified nacl-0abc123 at 2171234400. assigning ticket to sec-ops.
sec-ops: i'll own the ticket. we'll document the PCI exception, set automation to revert the NACL after 24h if scanner passes, and propose a long-term fix: route keystore traffic via a stable VPC endpoint IP or use an endpoint/private DNS to keep source IPs consistent.
maria: bootstrapping healthy after infra applied the NACL allow, 0 errors in the last 12 minutes. thanks all.
ops_sre: ACTIONS: [sec-ops] create ticket + exception justification, [infra] open PR to codify NACL exception + expiry tag, [infra] update iam role policy or add endpoint IPs, [finance] review cost impact and billback. marking P0 mitigated for now.
